claim: Murine Bbs4-/- islets show significantly lower intra-islet capillary density at eight weeks of age.
source: At eight weeks, murine Bbs4-/-islets show significantly lower intra-islet capillary density with enlarged diameters.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Murine Bbs4-/- islets show enlarged capillary diameters at eight weeks of age.
source: At eight weeks, murine Bbs4-/-islets show significantly lower intra-islet capillary density with enlarged diameters.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Transplanted Bbs4-/- islets exhibit delayed re-vascularization after engraftment.
source: Transplanted Bbs4-/- islets exhibit delayed re-vascularization and reduced vascular fenestration after engraftment, partially impairing vascular permeability and glucose delivery to β-cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by transplantation experiments and imaging data in the manuscript.

claim: Transplanted Bbs4-/- islets exhibit reduced vascular fenestration after engraftment.
source: Transplanted Bbs4-/- islets exhibit delayed re-vascularization and reduced vascular fenestration after engraftment, partially impairing vascular permeability and glucose delivery to β-cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by electron microscopy data in the manuscript.

claim: Reduced vascular fenestration in Bbs4-/- islets partially impairs vascular permeability.
source: Transplanted Bbs4-/- islets exhibit delayed re-vascularization and reduced vascular fenestration after engraftment, partially impairing vascular permeability and glucose delivery to β-cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by dextran leakage experiments in the manuscript.

claim: Reduced vascular fenestration in Bbs4-/- islets partially impairs glucose delivery to β-cells.
source: Transplanted Bbs4-/- islets exhibit delayed re-vascularization and reduced vascular fenestration after engraftment, partially impairing vascular permeability and glucose delivery to β-cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by 2-NBDG uptake experiments in the manuscript.

claim: Primary cilia on endothelial cells are the underlying cause of islet vascularization regulation via the VEGF-A/VEGFR2 pathway.
source: We identified primary cilia on endothelial cells as the underlying cause of this regulation, via the vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGF-A)/VEGF receptor 2 (VEGFR2) pathway.
evidence: The abstract states this conclusion, which is supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence including transplantation studies and in vitro experiments.

claim: In vitro silencing of ciliary genes in endothelial cells disrupts VEGF-A/VEGFR2 internalization.
source: In vitro silencing of ciliary genes in endothelial cells disrupts VEGF-A/VEGFR2 internalization and downstream signaling.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by cell culture experiments with shRNA knockdown.

claim: In vitro silencing of ciliary genes in endothelial cells disrupts VEGF-A/VEGFR2 downstream signaling.
source: In vitro silencing of ciliary genes in endothelial cells disrupts VEGF-A/VEGFR2 internalization and downstream signaling.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by Western blot analysis of signaling molecules.

claim: Key features of angiogenesis including proliferation are attenuated in human BBS4 silenced endothelial cells.
source: Consequently, key features of angiogenesis including proliferation and migration are attenuated in human BBS4 silenced endothelial cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by EdU incorporation assays.

claim: Key features of angiogenesis including migration are attenuated in human BBS4 silenced endothelial cells.
source: Consequently, key features of angiogenesis including proliferation and migration are attenuated in human BBS4 silenced endothelial cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by scratch assay experiments.

claim: Endothelial cell primary cilia regulate islet vascularization via the VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling pathway.
source: We conclude that endothelial cell primary cilia regulate islet vascularization and vascular barrier function via the VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling pathway.
evidence: The abstract states this conclusion, which is supported by the totality of experimental evidence presented.

claim: Endothelial cell primary cilia regulate vascular barrier function via the VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling pathway.
source: We conclude that endothelial cell primary cilia regulate islet vascularization and vascular barrier function via the VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling pathway.
evidence: The abstract states this conclusion, which is supported by permeability and fenestration experiments.

claim: Islet vascularization is essential for intact islet function and glucose homeostasis.
source: Islet vascularization is essential for intact islet function and glucose homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background knowledge.

claim: Primary cilia directly regulate insulin secretion.
source: We have previously shown that primary cilia directly regulate insulin secretion.
evidence: This is stated as a reference to previous work by the authors.

claim: Intra-islet capillary density was reduced by 35% in Bbs4-/- mice compared to wildtype littermate controls at 2 months of age.
source: Platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule (PECAM-1) immunofluorescence, as a marker of endothelial cells, revealed 35% reduced intra-islet capillary density compared to wildtype (wt) littermate controls (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This quantitative finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A,B showing immunofluorescence data.

claim: The relative PECAM-1 positive volume was normalized to insulin-positive islet volume to calculate intra-islet capillary density.
source: To calculate intra-islet capillary density, the relative PECAM-1 positive volume was normalized to insulin-positive islet volume (Figure 1B, p=0.0019).
evidence: This describes the methodology used for quantification.

claim: The average vessel diameter was increased by 18% in Bbs4-/- mice compared to wildtype controls at 2 months of age in cryosections.
source: In addition, the average vessel diameter was increased by 18% compared to that in wt controls (Figure 1C, p<0.0001).
evidence: This quantitative finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: Capillary density was reduced by 34% in freshly isolated islets of Bbs4-/- mice at 2 months of age.
source: In good agreement with our previous observations, capillary density was reduced by 34% and vessel diameter increased by 20% in islets of Bbs4-/- mice (p<0.0001 for both).
evidence: This finding from whole mount staining is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1D-F.

claim: Vessel diameter was increased by 20% in freshly isolated islets of Bbs4-/- mice at 2 months of age.
source: In good agreement with our previous observations, capillary density was reduced by 34% and vessel diameter increased by 20% in islets of Bbs4-/- mice (p<0.0001 for both).
evidence: This finding from whole mount staining is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1D-F.

claim: There was no change in pericyte coverage of intra-islet capillaries in Bbs4-/- mice based on NG2 immunofluorescence.
source: Of note, we observed no change in pericyte coverage of intra-islet capillaries based on Neuron-glial 2 (NG2) immunofluorescence (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B, p=0.7045).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: In 4-month-old Bbs4-/- mice, the difference in intra-islet capillary density approximated that of wildtype littermates.
source: In 4-month-old Bbs4-/- mice, however, the difference in intra-islet capillary density and diameter in Bbs4-/- mice approximated that of wt littermates (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–1E, p=0.0676 and 0.0736 respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: In 4-month-old Bbs4-/- mice, the difference in vessel diameter approximated that of wildtype littermates.
source: In 4-month-old Bbs4-/- mice, however, the difference in intra-islet capillary density and diameter in Bbs4-/- mice approximated that of wt littermates (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–1E, p=0.0676 and 0.0736 respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: There is no evidence of significant changes in β-cell mass in Bbs4-/- mice.
source: There is no evidence of significant changes in β-cell mass or insulin content in Bbs4-/- mice, and the observation of only slightly but not statistically significantly larger islets in Bbs4-/- mice at 4 weeks of age rules out effects of islet size on vessel density (Gerdes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: There is no evidence of significant changes in insulin content in Bbs4-/- mice.
source: There is no evidence of significant changes in β-cell mass or insulin content in Bbs4-/- mice, and the observation of only slightly but not statistically significantly larger islets in Bbs4-/- mice at 4 weeks of age rules out effects of islet size on vessel density (Gerdes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: Bbs4-/- mice have only slightly but not statistically significantly larger islets at 4 weeks of age.
source: There is no evidence of significant changes in β-cell mass or insulin content in Bbs4-/- mice, and the observation of only slightly but not statistically significantly larger islets in Bbs4-/- mice at 4 weeks of age rules out effects of islet size on vessel density (Gerdes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: Primary cilia and centrosome/basal body integrity play a role during the vascularization of pancreatic islets.
source: These dynamics implicate that primary cilia and centrosome/basal body integrity play a role during the vascularization of pancreatic islets.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temporal dynamics of vascular changes observed in the data.

claim: There was no detectable difference in vascularization of the exocrine portion of the pancreas at two months of age in Bbs4-/- mice.
source: Importantly, there was no detectable difference in vascularization of the exocrine portion of the pancreas at two months of age (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: Bbs4 function seems to be mostly restricted to the endocrine pancreas and not relevant for the exocrine compartment.
source: Therefore, Bbs4 function seems to be mostly restricted to the endocrine pancreas and not relevant for the exocrine compartment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential vascularization phenotype between endocrine and exocrine pancreas.

claim: Two weeks after transplantation, Bbs4-/- islets showed significantly less re-vascularization compared to wildtype controls.
source: Two weeks after transplantation, Bbs4-/- islets showed significantly less re-vascularization compared to wt controls (Figure 1H).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1H showing quantification of re-vascularization rates.

claim: Until four weeks after transplantation, re-vascularization of Bbs4-/- islets remains lower than that of wildtype islets.
source: Until four weeks after transplantation, re-vascularization remains lower than that of wt islets (Figure 1H).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1H.

claim: Twelve weeks post-transplantation, relative intra-islet vascular density is similar in both Bbs4-/- and wildtype islets.
source: Twelve weeks post-transplantation, relative intra-islet vascular density is similar in both Bbs4-/- and wt islets (Figure 1I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1I.

claim: The vessel diameter is greater in Bbs4-/- islets during the first four weeks of engraftment.
source: Morphologically, the newly formed blood vessels also differ among the two different genotypes during the first few weeks of engraftment. The vessel diameter is greater in Bbs4-/- islets, suggesting that there are fewer, wider islet capillaries in these islets compared to the wt controls during the first four weeks of engraftment (Figure 1J), similar to the results obtained from cryosections of young Bbs4-/- animals.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1J.

claim: There are fewer, wider islet capillaries in Bbs4-/- islets compared to wildtype controls during the first four weeks of engraftment.
source: The vessel diameter is greater in Bbs4-/- islets, suggesting that there are fewer, wider islet capillaries in these islets compared to the wt controls during the first four weeks of engraftment (Figure 1J), similar to the results obtained from cryosections of young Bbs4-/- animals.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the vessel diameter data.

claim: Endothelial cells disappear over prolonged periods of cultivation of isolated islets.
source: We and others have previously shown that endothelial cells disappear over prolonged periods of cultivation of isolated islets.
evidence: This is stated as a reference to previous work.

claim: Immediately after isolation, endothelial cells maintain the intra-islet capillary network.
source: Immediately after isolation, endothelial cells maintain the intra-islet capillary network.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: After two days in culture, endothelial cell clusters remain in isolated islets.
source: After two days in culture, endothelial cell clusters remain, whereas seven days post-isolation, intra-islet endothelial cells are generally lost (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: Seven days post-isolation, intra-islet endothelial cells are generally lost.
source: After two days in culture, endothelial cell clusters remain, whereas seven days post-isolation, intra-islet endothelial cells are generally lost (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: When transplanted shortly after isolation, a significant number of endothelial cells from the donor survives and contributes to revascularization of the islet graft.
source: Thus, when transplanted shortly after isolation, a significant number of endothelial cells from the donor survives and contributes to revascularization of the islet graft (Brissova et al., 2004; Linn et al., 2003; Nyqvist et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to previous publications.

claim: Both islet cells and endothelial cells are ciliated.
source: Importantly, both islet cells and endothelial cells are ciliated (Nauli et al., 2008; Dinsmore and Reiter, 2016; Hughes et al., 2020; Ma and Zhou, 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to previous publications.

claim: Islets cultivated for seven days before transplantation favor almost exclusively revascularization by the recipients' vascular system.
source: In the other experimental setting, islets were kept in culture for seven days after isolation before being transplanted to the ACE of wt recipients. This treatment ablates endothelial cells in the donor tissue and favors almost exclusively revascularization by the recipients' vascular system (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, lower panel).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the experimental design illustrated in the supplementary figure.

claim: No significant differences in re-vascularization rate over time were observed when islets were cultured for seven days before transplantation.
source: We did not observe significant differences in re-vascularization rate over time or islet vascular density at the twelve-week endpoint (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A-C.

claim: No significant differences in islet vascular density at the twelve-week endpoint were observed when islets were cultured for seven days before transplantation.
source: We did not observe significant differences in re-vascularization rate over time or islet vascular density at the twelve-week endpoint (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A-C.

claim: Vessel morphology and diameter were similar in Bbs4-/- and wildtype control islets when cultured for seven days before transplantation.
source: In addition, vessel morphology and diameter were similar in Bbs4-/- and wt control islets (Figure 2D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2D.

claim: The majority of donor endothelial cells were lost during the seven-day cultivation.
source: Importantly, under these experimental conditions, the majority of donor endothelial cells were lost during the seven-day cultivation.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental conditions.

claim: Bbs4-/- endothelial cells underlie the blunted angiogenic response, thus impeding islet re-vascularization.
source: In conclusion, our findings suggest that Bbs4-/- endothelial cells underlie the blunted angiogenic response, thus impeding islet re-vascularization.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential effects observed with different culture durations.

claim: Significantly slower re-vascularization was observed when wildtype islets were transplanted to Bbs4-/- recipients.
source: Indeed, we observed significantly slower re-vascularization in this transplantation scheme and the rates correlated with the time islets were kept in culture (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3D and E.

claim: The re-vascularization rate of wildtype islets transplanted to Bbs4-/- mice seven days post-isolation was significantly lower than that of wildtype islets two days post-isolation.
source: The re-vascularization rate of wt islets transplanted to the ACE of Bbs4-/- mice seven days post-isolation was significantly lower than that of wt islets two days post-isolation (p=0.0053), and both were significantly lower than that of wt islets transplanted to wt ACE (p=0.0002 for two-day group and p<0.0001 for seven-day group respectively).
evidence: This quantitative comparison is stated in the text with statistical values.

claim: Intra-islet vessel density after completion of re-vascularization was not significantly lower in wildtype islets transplanted into Bbs4-/- recipients than in wildtype islets transplanted into wildtype recipients at the twelve-week endpoint.
source: Interestingly, intra-islet vessel density after completion of re-vascularization was not significantly lower than that of wt islets transplanted into wt recipients at the twelve-week endpoint (Figure 3F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3F.

claim: The diameter of intra-islet capillaries was markedly wider in wildtype islets transplanted to Bbs4-/- recipients after seven days in culture than the other two groups.
source: The diameter of intra-islet capillaries, however, was markedly wider in wt islets transplanted to Bbs4-/- recipients after seven days in culture than the other two groups (Figure 3G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3G.

claim: Donor endothelial cells constituted 40 ± 3% of the newly formed vasculature between three to five weeks post-transplantation in freshly transplanted islets under the kidney capsule.
source: This is in good agreement with another study, in which freshly transplanted islets were under the kidney capsule; here, the authors observed that donor endothelial cells constituted 40 ± 3% of the newly formed vasculature between three to five weeks post-transplantation (Brissova et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to a previous study.

claim: The ratio of recipient-derived tdTomato-positive endothelial cells stayed significantly higher in Bbs4-/- islets during the first four weeks of engraftment.
source: While delayed re-vascularization and altered vascular morphology of Bbs4-/- islets was observed as before in wt recipients (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and E, Figure 1H and J), the ratio of recipient-derived tdTomato-positive endothelial cells stayed significantly higher in Bbs4-/- islets during the first four weeks of engraftment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: Bbs4-/- endothelial cells are less responsive to the angiogenic signals than wildtype endothelial cells.
source: Taken together, these results support the conclusion that Bbs4-/- endothelial cells are indeed less responsive to the angiogenic signals than wt endothelial cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transplantation experiments with tdTomato-labeled endothelial cells.

claim: Pifo-/- mice have dysfunctional cilia that cannot be properly disassembled.
source: Pitchfork (Pifo-/-) mice have dysfunctional cilia that cannot be properly disassembled (Kinzel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: PIFO does not localize to the ciliary axoneme but accumulates at the base of the cilium during cilia disassembly.
source: PIFO does not localize to the ciliary axoneme but accumulates at the base of the cilium during cilia disassembly and interacts with ciliary targeting complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the text as background information about PIFO function.

claim: Laterality defects in Pifo-/- mice suggest that ciliary signaling is impaired in these animals.
source: Laterality defects in Pifo-/- mice suggest that ciliary signaling is impaired in these animals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed phenotype.

claim: Intra-islet vascular density was reduced by 19% in 3-month-old Pifo-/- mice compared to littermate controls.
source: PECAM-1 staining revealed 19% reduction in intra-islet vascular density and 38% increase in vessel diameter in Pifo-/- mice compared to littermate controls, similar to our observation in Bbs4-/- islets (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–2C, p=0.0421 and p=0.0032 respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: Vessel diameter was increased by 38% in 3-month-old Pifo-/- mice compared to littermate controls.
source: PECAM-1 staining revealed 19% reduction in intra-islet vascular density and 38% increase in vessel diameter in Pifo-/- mice compared to littermate controls, similar to our observation in Bbs4-/- islets (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–2C, p=0.0421 and p=0.0032 respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: Transplantation of Pifo-/- islets into wildtype ACE showed a delay in relative re-vascularization compared to wildtype islets.
source: Transplantation of Pifo-/- islets into wt ACE showed a delay in relative re-vascularization compared to wt islets, also similar to what we observed for Bbs4-/- mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D–2G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: The effects on re-vascularization were less severe in Pifo-/- islets than in Bbs4-/- islets.
source: Although the effects on re-vascularization were less severe than those in Bbs4-/- islets, the findings support a role for primary cilia in islet vascularization and the angiogenic response in islet engraftment.
evidence: This is a comparison of the phenotypic severity between two mutant models.

claim: The findings from Pifo-/- mice support a role for primary cilia in islet vascularization and the angiogenic response in islet engraftment.
source: Although the effects on re-vascularization were less severe than those in Bbs4-/- islets, the findings support a role for primary cilia in islet vascularization and the angiogenic response in islet engraftment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Pifo-/- data.

claim: Ift88 is essential to ciliary maintenance and formation.
source: Ift88 is essential to ciliary maintenance and formation, and cells depleted of Ift88 do not have ciliary axonemes (Davenport et al., 2007), although the early stages of ciliogenesis such as vesicle docking to centrosomes are still completed (Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to previous publications.

claim: Cells depleted of Ift88 do not have ciliary axonemes.
source: Ift88 is essential to ciliary maintenance and formation, and cells depleted of Ift88 do not have ciliary axonemes (Davenport et al., 2007), although the early stages of ciliogenesis such as vesicle docking to centrosomes are still completed (Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: The early stages of ciliogenesis such as vesicle docking to centrosomes are still completed in Ift88-depleted cells.
source: Ift88 is essential to ciliary maintenance and formation, and cells depleted of Ift88 do not have ciliary axonemes (Davenport et al., 2007), although the early stages of ciliogenesis such as vesicle docking to centrosomes are still completed (Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: No observable difference in intra-islet vascular density was found between induced βICKO mice and oil-treated controls.
source: We found no observable difference between induced βICKO mice and oil-treated controls (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B and C.

claim: No differences in the re-vascularization rate were observed between vehicle and Tamoxifen-treated βICKO islets.
source: We did not observe differences in the re-vascularization rate between vehicle and Tamoxifen-treated βICKO islets (Figure 4D–G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4D-G.

claim: Cilia in endothelial cells regulate re-vascularization during islet engraftment.
source: Overall, our observations strongly suggest that cilia in endothelial cells regulate re-vascularization during islet engraftment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the βICKO experiments showing no effect of β-cell cilia deletion.

claim: Fenestration was significantly reduced by 27% in the capillaries of Bbs4-/- compared to wildtype islet grafts in the ACE four months after transplantation.
source: Blinded analysis of electron micrographs showed significantly reduced fenestration in the capillaries of Bbs4-/- compared to wt islet grafts in the ACE four months after transplantation (Figure 5A and B, 27% lower, p=0.0006).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 5A and B.

claim: The basement membrane seems slightly thicker in Bbs4-/- islets, but no significant thickening was observed.
source: Although the basement membrane seems slightly thicker in Bbs4-/- islets, we did not observe significant thickening of this structure (Figure 5C, p=0.1414).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: Both the initial rate and the plateau of fluorescence intensity are decreased in Bbs4-/- islet grafts after 40 kDa dextran injection.
source: Importantly, both the initial rate and the plateau are decreased in Bbs4-/- islet grafts (Figure 5E, p=0.0478).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5E showing dextran leakage kinetics.

claim: Simulation of the dye leakage process supports different kinetics of dye leakage between wildtype and Bbs4-/- islets.
source: Simulation of this process also supports different kinetics of dye leakage (Figure 5F), suggesting that the delivery of medium sized molecules out of the blood stream is less efficient in Bbs4-/- intra islet capillaries.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5F showing simulated curves.

claim: The delivery of medium sized molecules out of the blood stream is less efficient in Bbs4-/- intra-islet capillaries.
source: Simulation of this process also supports different kinetics of dye leakage (Figure 5F), suggesting that the delivery of medium sized molecules out of the blood stream is less efficient in Bbs4-/- intra islet capillaries.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the dextran leakage data.

claim: Wildtype islet cells internalized significantly more 2-NBDG than Bbs4-/- islet cells under the same period of time.
source: Importantly, wt islet cells internalized significantly more 2-NBDG than Bbs4-/- islet cells under the same period of time (Figure 5H, p=0.0118).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5H showing 2-NBDG uptake kinetics.

claim: Ciliary/basal body proteins play a critical role in maintaining islet capillary fenestration with implications for the delivery of glucose and potentially other nutrients to islet cells.
source: This result points to a critical role of ciliary/basal body proteins in maintaining islet capillary fenestration with implications for the delivery of glucose and potentially other nutrients to islet cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 2-NBDG uptake data.

claim: 100 islets (diameter between 150 and 200 μm) transplanted into the ACE of chemically induced diabetic mice were sufficient to revert blood glucose concentration to normoglycemic levels.
source: It was previously shown that 100 islets (diameter between 150 and 200 μm) transplanted into the ACE of chemically induced diabetic mice were sufficient to revert blood glucose concentration to normoglycemic levels. This amount of pancreatic islets is defined as marginal islet mass (Rodriguez-Diaz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: Four weeks after transplantation, mice transplanted with Bbs4-/- islets were glucose intolerant compared to those mice transplanted with wildtype islets.
source: Four weeks after transplantation, mice transplanted with Bbs4-/- islets were glucose intolerant compared to those mice transplanted with wt islets (Figure 5I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5I showing glucose tolerance test results.

claim: Eight weeks after transplantation, mice transplanted with Bbs4-/- islets showed impaired glucose tolerance.
source: Eight weeks after transplantation, mice showed impaired glucose tolerance and, 12 weeks post-transplantation, only mildly impaired glucose handling compared to those transplanted with wt islets (Figure 5J and K).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5J.

claim: Twelve weeks post-transplantation, mice transplanted with Bbs4-/- islets showed only mildly impaired glucose handling compared to those transplanted with wildtype islets.
source: Eight weeks after transplantation, mice showed impaired glucose tolerance and, 12 weeks post-transplantation, only mildly impaired glucose handling compared to those transplanted with wt islets (Figure 5J and K).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5K.

claim: The phenotype is ameliorated over time, which is consistent with observations in re-vascularization.
source: Overall, the phenotype is ameliorated over time, which is consistent with our previous observations in re-vascularization (Figures 1 and 2), suggesting that a lack of capillaries in Bbs4-/- islets indeed negatively affects whole body glucose homeostasis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temporal dynamics of glucose tolerance.

claim: A lack of capillaries in Bbs4-/- islets negatively affects whole body glucose homeostasis.
source: Overall, the phenotype is ameliorated over time, which is consistent with our previous observations in re-vascularization (Figures 1 and 2), suggesting that a lack of capillaries in Bbs4-/- islets indeed negatively affects whole body glucose homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the glucose tolerance test data.

claim: Glucose handling is mildly impaired by the end of 12 weeks, which is probably caused by impaired vascular barrier function in combination with defective 1st phase insulin secretion.
source: Glucose handling is mildly impaired by the end of 12 weeks, which is probably caused by impaired vascular barrier function in combination with defective 1st phase insulin secretion (Gerdes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the glucose tolerance data with reference to previous work.

claim: Suppressing Bbs4 by RNA interference reduces Bbs4 expression up to two-fold in MS-1 cells.
source: Suppressing Bbs4 by RNA interference reduces Bbs4 expression up to two-fold (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: Expression analysis of key angiogenic factors revealed no observable changes in Tie1, Tie2, eNOS or Dll4 in Bbs4-depleted MS-1 cells.
source: Expression analysis of key angiogenic factors revealed no observable changes in Tie1, Tie2, endothelial Nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) or Notch ligand Delta-4 (Dll4) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A showing qPCR data.

claim: VEGFR2 is downregulated by 20% when MS-1 cells are depleted of Bbs4.
source: However, VEGFR2, Ephrin A1 and B2 are downregulated by 20% when MS-1 cells are depleted of Bbs4.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: Ephrin A1 is downregulated by 20% when MS-1 cells are depleted of Bbs4.
source: However, VEGFR2, Ephrin A1 and B2 are downregulated by 20% when MS-1 cells are depleted of Bbs4.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: Ephrin B2 is downregulated by 20% when MS-1 cells are depleted of Bbs4.
source: However, VEGFR2, Ephrin A1 and B2 are downregulated by 20% when MS-1 cells are depleted of Bbs4.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: Intra-islet capillary density and fenestration is primarily maintained by VEGFA-VEGFR2-signaling.
source: Of note, intra-islet capillary density and fenestration is primarily maintained by VEGFA-VEGFR2-signaling (Lammert et al., 2003; Esser et al., 1998; Roberts and Palade, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to previous publications.

claim: In control cells, VEGFR2 Tyr 1175 phosphorylation is markedly increased at seven minutes (4.3-fold) after VEGF-A stimulation.
source: In control cells (scrambled), VEGFR2 Tyr 1175 phosphorylation is markedly increased at seven minutes (4.3-fold) and sustained until 15 min (3.4-fold) after stimulation (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6B and D.

claim: In control cells, VEGFR2 Tyr 1175 phosphorylation is sustained until 15 min (3.4-fold) after VEGF-A stimulation.
source: In control cells (scrambled), VEGFR2 Tyr 1175 phosphorylation is markedly increased at seven minutes (4.3-fold) and sustained until 15 min (3.4-fold) after stimulation (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6B and D.

claim: pTyr1175 levels increased minimally in BBS4-depleted HDMECs (2-fold and 1.8-fold at 7 and 15 minutes respectively).
source: By comparison, pTyr1175 levels increased minimally in BBS4-depleted HDMECs (2-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively, Figure 6B and D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6B and D.

claim: Total levels of VEGFR2 are lowered in absence of Bbs4 by 20%.
source: At the same time, total levels of VEGFR2 are also lowered in absence of Bbs4 by 20% (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, p=0.0101).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data.

claim: EphrinB2 protein level is slightly reduced by 5% in BBS4-depleted HDMECs.
source: In addition, we found that EphrinB2 protein level is slightly reduced in BBS4-depleted HDMECs (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplements 1B and 5%, p=0.0051), corroborating our previous finding of decreased gene expression (Figure 6A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data.

claim: Loss of Bbs4 leads to a 40% attenuation in PLCγ1 phosphorylation at seven minutes after VEGF-A stimulation.
source: While PLCγ1 phosphorylation peaks at seven minutes and decreases 15 min after stimulation in control cells, loss of Bbs4 leads to a 40% attenuation in PLCγ1 phosphorylation at seven minutes (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, p=0.0336).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data.

claim: pAkt was significantly reduced in BBS4-depleted cells seven and fifteen minutes after VEGF-A addition.
source: Similarly, pAkt and pMAPK 42/44 were significantly reduced in BBS4-depleted cells seven and fifteen minutes after VEGF-A addition (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, p=0.0222 and p=0.0010, respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data.

claim: pMAPK 42/44 was significantly reduced in BBS4-depleted cells seven and fifteen minutes after VEGF-A addition.
source: Similarly, pAkt and pMAPK 42/44 were significantly reduced in BBS4-depleted cells seven and fifteen minutes after VEGF-A addition (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, p=0.0222 and p=0.0010, respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data.

claim: In unstimulated islet cells, pAkt and pMAPK baseline levels did not differ between wildtype and Bbs4-/- cells.
source: In unstimulated islet cells, pAkt and pMAPK baseline levels did not differ between wt and Bbs4-/- cells.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in supplementary figures.

claim: Ten minutes after addition of 100 ng/ml VEGF-A, pAkt levels increased 2.2-fold in wildtype but only 1.4-fold in Bbs4-/- islet cells.
source: Ten minutes after addition of 100 ng/ml VEGF-A, pAkt levels increased 2.2-fold in wt but only 1.4-fold in Bbs4-/- cells.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in supplementary figures.

claim: Ten minutes after addition of 100 ng/ml VEGF-A, pMAPK levels increased 3-fold in wildtype but only 1.5-fold in Bbs4-/- islet cells.
source: Likewise, pMAPK levels increased 3-fold in wt but only 1.5-fold in Bbs4-/- cells, demonstrating that VEGF-A triggered downstream signaling is not sufficiently activated in these cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in supplementary figures.

claim: VEGF-A triggered downstream signaling is not sufficiently activated in Bbs4-/- islet cells.
source: Likewise, pMAPK levels increased 3-fold in wt but only 1.5-fold in Bbs4-/- cells, demonstrating that VEGF-A triggered downstream signaling is not sufficiently activated in these cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Western blot data.

claim: Wildtype islets cultured for seven days showed markedly lower response to VEGF-A stimulation.
source: Importantly, similar experiments on wt islets cultured for seven days to diminish intra-islet endothelial cells showed markedly lower response to VEGF-A stimulation; therefore, VEGF-A/VEGFR2 dependent signaling cascades in endothelial cells contribute significantly to overall VEGF-A dependent signaling in whole murine islets (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in supplementary figures.

claim: VEGF-A/VEGFR2 dependent signaling cascades in endothelial cells contribute significantly to overall VEGF-A dependent signaling in whole murine islets.
source: Importantly, similar experiments on wt islets cultured for seven days to diminish intra-islet endothelial cells showed markedly lower response to VEGF-A stimulation; therefore, VEGF-A/VEGFR2 dependent signaling cascades in endothelial cells contribute significantly to overall VEGF-A dependent signaling in whole murine islets (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of fresh and cultured islets.

claim: Binding of VEGF-A to receptors triggers their endocytosis instantly.
source: Binding of VEGF-A to receptors triggers their endocytosis instantly, which is the initial step for subsequent intracellular signaling, and mainly regulated by EphrinB2 (Sawamiphak et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2010; Nakayama et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to previous publications.

claim: VEGFR2 endocytosis is mainly regulated by EphrinB2.
source: Binding of VEGF-A to receptors triggers their endocytosis instantly, which is the initial step for subsequent intracellular signaling, and mainly regulated by EphrinB2 (Sawamiphak et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2010; Nakayama et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to previous publications.

claim: VEGFR2 does not signal from the plasma membrane but from other intracellular compartments, mainly early endosomes and the ESCRT.
source: Several studies have shown that VEGFR2 does not signal from the plasma membrane but from other intracellular compartments, mainly early endosomes and the endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) (Nakayama et al., 2013; Bruns et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to previous publications.

claim: After 30 min incubation, BBS4-depleted HDMECs had only internalized 45% VEGF-A compared to controls.
source: After 30 min incubation, BBS4-depleted cells had only internalized 45% VEGF-A compared to controls (Figure 6E and F, p=0.0101).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6E and F showing biotinylated VEGF-A uptake.

claim: Ift88-depleted MS-1 cells internalized 61% VEGF-A compared to controls after 30 min.
source: Similar to our observations in HDMECs, control MS-1 cells efficiently and rapidly internalized VEGF-A, while by comparison, Ift88-depleted MS-1 cells internalized less VEGF-A after 30 min (61% compared to controls, Figure 6—figure supplement 1H–1J, p=0.0027).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by supplementary figure data.

claim: 25% more VEGFR2 remained on the cell surface in BBS4-silenced cells after ten min incubation with VEGF-A, indicating decreased internalization of VEGFR2.
source: After ten min incubation with VEGF-A, a significant number of VEGFR2 was internalized in control cells, while 25% more VEGFR2 remained on the cell surface in BBS4-silenced cells, which indicates decreased internalization of VEGFR2 (Figure 6H, p=0.0019) and may be explained by our previous finding of lowered EphrinB2 levels (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6H showing cell surface VEGFR2 staining.

claim: The VEGFR2 internalization upon ligand binding is regulated by ciliary and basal body proteins.
source: These results suggest that the VEGFR2 internalization upon ligand binding is regulated by ciliary and basal body proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the VEGF-A and VEGFR2 internalization experiments.

claim: VEGF-A induced cell proliferation in Bbs4-depleted MS-1 cells was reduced by 27% compared to control cells.
source: Under the chosen conditions, VEGF-A induced cell proliferation in Bbs4-depleted cells was reduced by 27% compared to controls cells (Figure 6I and J, p=0.0024).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6I and J showing EdU incorporation assay.

claim: Bbs4-depleted MS-1 cells covered only 73% of the distance of control cells in the same time frame in a scratch assay.
source: A scratch assay revealed that Bbs4-depleted cells covered only 73% of the distance of control cells in the same time frame (Figure 6K, p<0.0001), similar to previous reports of ciliary involvement in cell migration (Vion et al., 2018).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6K showing migration assay results.

claim: Cilia and basal body proteins play a role in VEGF-A/VEGFR2 dependent regulation of endothelial cell function.
source: These independent lines of evidence, i.e. reduced endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and impaired vessel fenestration, all point to a role for cilia and basal body proteins in VEGF-A/VEGFR2 dependent regulation of endothelial cell function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Notch1 is an important negative regulator of VEGF-A dependent signaling.
source: An important negative regulator of VEGF-A dependent signaling is Notch1 –dependent signaling (Williams et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to a previous publication.

claim: The Notch1 intracellular domain elicited a weaker response in Ift88 depleted MS-1 cells compared to controls.
source: Placing firefly luciferase under the control of multimerized CSL response elements upstream of a minimal promoter showed that the Notch1 intracellular domain (NICD) elicited a weaker response in Ift88 depleted cells compared to controls.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by luciferase assay data in supplementary figures.

claim: Loss of Notch1 signaling cannot explain the observed vascular phenotype.
source: Because Notch1 signaling is a negative regulator of VEGF-A dependent signaling, loss of Notch1 signaling cannot explain the observed phenotype.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the regulatory relationship between Notch1 and VEGF-A signaling.

claim: VEGF-A expression was reduced by 20% in Bbs4-/- islets compared to wildtype controls.
source: We also examined the relative expression of the same set of angiogenic factors in freshly isolated islets and found, while most expression levels remain unchanged, VEGF-A expression was reduced by 20% in Bbs4-/- islets compared to wt controls.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by qPCR data in supplementary figures.

claim: Von-Hippel-Lindau gene expression remains unchanged in Bbs4-/- islets.
source: Von-Hippel-Lindau gene expression, a known ciliary protein mutated in Von Hippel-Lindau disease and a known regulator of Hypoxia induced factor 1a, remains unchanged (Figure 6—figure supplement 1L).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by qPCR data in supplementary figures.

claim: VEGF-A gene expression was slightly decreased in βICKO islets.
source: VEGF-A gene expression was also slightly decreased in βICKO islets (Figure 6—figure supplement 1M).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by qPCR data in supplementary figures.

claim: Loss of Bbs4 function decreased VEGF-A secretion by 33%.
source: Loss of Bbs4 or Ift88 function respectively decreased VEGF-A secretion by 33% and 28% (Figure 6—figure supplement 1N, p=0.0063 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1O, p=0.0070), which could be explained by the reduction in VEGF-A gene expression.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in supplementary figures.

claim: Loss of Ift88 function decreased VEGF-A secretion by 28%.
source: Loss of Bbs4 or Ift88 function respectively decreased VEGF-A secretion by 33% and 28% (Figure 6—figure supplement 1N, p=0.0063 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1O, p=0.0070), which could be explained by the reduction in VEGF-A gene expression.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in supplementary figures.

claim: The intra-islet VEGF-A signaling pathway is impaired in Bbs4-/- islets.
source: Altogether, these results consistently suggest that the intra-islet VEGF-A signaling pathway is impaired in Bbs4-/- islets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression and secretion data.

claim: Pancreatic islets rely on their morphologically unique vascular network for functional support and efficient delivery of oxygen and nutrients.
source: Pancreatic islets rely on their morphologically unique vascular network for functional support and efficient delivery of oxygen and nutrients, as well as rapid dissemination of islet derived hormones.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background knowledge.

claim: Blood vessels are important to establish microenvironments or 'niches' required for stem or progenitor cell maintenance.
source: In addition, blood vessels are important to establish microenvironments or 'niches' required for stem or progenitor cell maintenance (Brissova et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: Proper islet re-vascularization has been suggested to be a critical determinant in graft survival following islet transplantation in the treatment of Type 1 Diabetes.
source: Proper islet re-vascularization has also been suggested to be a critical determinant in graft survival following islet transplantation in the treatment of Type 1 Diabetes (Vaithilingam et al., 2008; Brissova et al., 2006; Brissova et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with references to previous publications.

claim: Vascular endothelial cells in both central and peripheral organs of insulin action have been implicated in insulin resistance.
source: As the functional barrier between tissues and the blood stream, vascular endothelial cells in both central and peripheral organs of insulin action have been implicated in insulin resistance (Konishi et al., 2017) and diabetes etiology (Goligorsky, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with references to previous publications.

claim: Vascular endothelial cells have been implicated in diabetes etiology.
source: As the functional barrier between tissues and the blood stream, vascular endothelial cells in both central and peripheral organs of insulin action have been implicated in insulin resistance (Konishi et al., 2017) and diabetes etiology (Goligorsky, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: The exocrine pancreas is organized by branching ducts.
source: Anatomically, the exocrine pancreas is organized by branching ducts while the endocrine islets of Langerhans are scattered throughout the exocrine tissue and interconnected by blood vessels (Cleaver and Dor, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: The endocrine islets of Langerhans are scattered throughout the exocrine tissue and interconnected by blood vessels.
source: Anatomically, the exocrine pancreas is organized by branching ducts while the endocrine islets of Langerhans are scattered throughout the exocrine tissue and interconnected by blood vessels (Cleaver and Dor, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: Pancreatic bud and blood vessel formation are initiated at the same time during development.
source: During development, pancreatic bud and blood vessel formation are initiated at the same time and, although both endocrine and exocrine pancreatic tissue are derived from the same progenitors, vessel density in the exocrine portion of the organ is five times lower compared to intra-islet vessel density after maturity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background knowledge.

claim: Vessel density in the exocrine portion of the pancreas is five times lower compared to intra-islet vessel density after maturity.
source: During development, pancreatic bud and blood vessel formation are initiated at the same time and, although both endocrine and exocrine pancreatic tissue are derived from the same progenitors, vessel density in the exocrine portion of the organ is five times lower compared to intra-islet vessel density after maturity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background knowledge.

claim: Islet capillaries have ten times more diaphragm-covered fenestrae than the exocrine pancreas.
source: Moreover, islet capillaries have ten times more diaphragm-covered fenestrae than the exocrine pancreas- a distinctive feature that facilitates rapid exchange of fluids and small solutes between tissue and blood stream (Kolka and Bergman, 2012; Henderson and Moss, 1985).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with references to previous publications.

claim: Specific local factors play a role in endocrine pancreatic vascularization.
source: This suggests that specific local factors play a role in endocrine pancreatic vascularization.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differences in vascularization between endocrine and exocrine pancreas.

claim: VEGF-A is produced by islet endocrine cells (both α- and β-cells).
source: VEGF-A is produced by islet endocrine cells (both α- and β-cells) and binds to VEGFR2 on endothelial cells, which is crucial for the maintenance of a dense and leaky islet microvasculature (Brissova et al., 2006; Lammert et al., 2003; Christofori et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with references to previous publications.

claim: VEGF-A binds to VEGFR2 on endothelial cells, which is crucial for the maintenance of a dense and leaky islet microvasculature.
source: VEGF-A is produced by islet endocrine cells (both α- and β-cells) and binds to VEGFR2 on endothelial cells, which is crucial for the maintenance of a dense and leaky islet microvasculature (Brissova et al., 2006; Lammert et al., 2003; Christofori et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with references to previous publications.

claim: Pancreas-specific VEGF-A ablation does not completely block islet vascularization.
source: While pancreas-specific VEGF-A ablation does not completely block islet vascularization, islet fenestration is crucially dependent on VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background knowledge.

claim: Islet fenestration is crucially dependent on VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling.
source: While pancreas-specific VEGF-A ablation does not completely block islet vascularization, islet fenestration is crucially dependent on VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background knowledge.

claim: Delivery of nutrients to β-cells and disposal of insulin into the blood vessels is modulated by fenestrated blood vessels that are fine tuning the system to optimize glucose tolerance.
source: Delivery of nutrients to β-cells and disposal of insulin into the blood vessels is modulated by fenestrated blood vessels that are fine tuning the system to optimize glucose tolerance (Lammert et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: β-cell-specific Vegfa deficient mice are severely glucose intolerant but show normal glucose response and insulin secretion in isolated islets.
source: β-cell-specific Vegfa deficient mice are severely glucose intolerant but show normal glucose response and insulin secretion in isolated islets, suggesting that either nutrients (such as glucose) are not delivered efficiently to the β-cells or insulin disposal into the blood stream is significantly hampered in vivo (Brissova et al., 2006; Lammert et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with references to previous publications.

claim: In β-cell-specific Vegfa deficient mice, either nutrients (such as glucose) are not delivered efficiently to the β-cells or insulin disposal into the blood stream is significantly hampered in vivo.
source: β-cell-specific Vegfa deficient mice are severely glucose intolerant but show normal glucose response and insulin secretion in isolated islets, suggesting that either nutrients (such as glucose) are not delivered efficiently to the β-cells or insulin disposal into the blood stream is significantly hampered in vivo (Brissova et al., 2006; Lammert et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the phenotype observed in previous studies.

claim: Removal of Vegfa from mature β-cells at a later stage has a less severe impact on glucose tolerance although intra-islet capillary density is reduced by 50%.
source: In contrast, removal of Vegfa from mature β-cells at a later stage has a less severe impact on glucose tolerance although intra-islet capillary density is reduced by 50% (Reinert et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: After islet maturation, local VEGF-A/VEGFR2 dependent signaling is less important for the maintenance of intra-islet capillaries and insulin disposal compared to during development.
source: This may suggest that, after islet maturation, local VEGF-A/VEGFR2 dependent signaling is less important for the maintenance of intra-islet capillaries and insulin disposal compared to during development.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential effects of VEGF-A deletion at different developmental stages.

claim: Deletion of Integrin-linked kinase (Ilk) specifically blocks intra-islet capillary formation completely and leads to glucose intolerance.
source: Changing the biomechanical properties such as actomyosin cortex tension of epithelial cells in developing islets by deletion of Integrin-linked kinase (Ilk) specifically blocks intra-islet capillary formation completely and leads to glucose intolerance.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: In Ilk-deleted islets, blood vessels accumulate in the islet periphery and form an envelope-like structure.
source: Instead, blood vessels accumulate in the islet periphery and form an envelope-like structure suggesting that biomechanics of epithelial tissues are important determinants of blood vessel formation (Kragl et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: Biomechanics of epithelial tissues are important determinants of blood vessel formation.
source: Instead, blood vessels accumulate in the islet periphery and form an envelope-like structure suggesting that biomechanics of epithelial tissues are important determinants of blood vessel formation (Kragl et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: Primary cilia are present on roughly eighty percent of the cells in the adult mammalian organism.
source: Primary cilia are present on roughly eighty percent of the cells in the adult mammalian organism (Wheatley et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

claim: In metabolically active organs, primary cilia play a role in sensing metabolic signals and energy homeostasis.
source: In metabolically active organs, they play a role in sensing metabolic signals and energy homeostasis (Oh et al., 2015; Volta and Gerdes, 2017).

claim: β-cell cilia play a role in insulin signaling, insulin secretion and glucose homeostasis.

source: Endothelial cells are also ciliated, and endothelial cilia have been implicated in flow-sensing and vascular hypertension, intracranial blood vessel formation, and atherosclerosis prevention (Nauli et al., 2008; Nauli et al., 2011; Kallakuri et al., 2015; Dinsmore and Reiter, 2016).

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with references to previous publications.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to a previous publication.

source: Bbs4-/- mice are a model of Bardet-Biedl Syndrome (OMIM #209900), a ciliopathy characterized mainly by polydactyly, renal and gonadal malformations and truncal obesity.

claim: Bardet-Biedl Syndrome is a ciliopathy characterized mainly by polydactyly, renal and gonadal malformations and truncal obesity.
source: Bbs4-/- mice are a model of Bardet-Biedl Syndrome (OMIM #209900), a ciliopathy characterized mainly by polydactyly, renal and gonadal malformations and truncal obesity.

claim: Bbs4 encodes a protein that is a component of the BBSome complex.
source: Bbs4 encodes a protein that is a component of the BBSome complex, a protein super complex thought to be involved in the sorting of membrane proteins to and from the ciliary compartment (Nachury et al., 2007; Liew et al., 2014).

claim: The BBSome complex is thought to be involved in the sorting of membrane proteins to and from the ciliary compartment.
source: Bbs4 encodes a protein that is a component of the BBSome complex, a protein super complex thought to be involved in the sorting of membrane proteins to and from the ciliary compartment (Nachury et al., 2007; Liew et al., 2014).
